assignments.brief_reason: Sets removal threshold only for extremely demeaning/hate-adjacent content, not for mere insensitivity.
Claims the pair didn’t influence them, framing low influence via general free-speech stance.
Mentions First Amendment framing based on reading both versions; not explicitly a non-influence/independence claim.
Says no moderation needed for ordinary opinions/exaggeration; doesn’t clearly specify harm/toxicity thresholds.
Uses content-style/quality threshold (good faith) while disallowing angry name-calling/violent rhetoric.
Anti-silencing rationale; not primarily about harm/toxicity thresholds.
Says mirrored pairs made a joint decision easy and thus had limited additional influence.
Explicit free-speech bounds test with buffers; removal tied to crossing into hate speech and malicious misinformation.
Explicitly says they ignored pair political positions as the basis for decisions.
Claims opposition in the pair didn’t change underlying intent; relied on independent checks.
Task-goal/healthy-conversation framing for removal; not clearly mapped to harm/toxicity threshold definition.
Uses the pair to check truth across sides, which is not captured by the low-influence or harm-threshold themes.
Process meta about avoiding bias/neutrality rather than explicit harm thresholds or pair non-influence.
Neutrality goal (not leaning left/right) during evaluation; not primarily harm-threshold or pair non-influence.
Absolutist free-speech stance with removal only when there is physical harm/threat.
Allows unless posts seem like a threat or act of violence, making harm a key threshold.
Swearing tolerated; removal depends on harmful/misdirected usage rather than profanity alone (toxic/harm framing implied).
Aims for balanced evaluation across far-reaching viewpoints; not specifically non-influence or harm threshold.
Foul language targeting/harassment drives removal despite free-speech values, using a harm/harassment-like threshold.
States decision was not really influenced by the pair, relying on a general entitlement-to-opinion norm.
